claim: Adult neurogenesis occurs in the olfactory bulb (OB) of rodents.
source: Neurogenesis continues after birth in the hippocampus and olfactory bulb of rodents.
evidence: This is stated as established fact in the introduction without qualification.

claim: During OB neurogenesis, predetermined stem cell populations along the walls of forebrain ventricles generate neuronal precursors.
source: During OB neurogenesis predetermined stem cell population along the walls of forebrain ventricles generate neuronal precursors that migrate via the rostral migratory stream (RMS) into the center of the OB.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about the neurogenesis process.

claim: Neuronal precursors migrate via the rostral migratory stream (RMS) into the center of the OB.
source: During OB neurogenesis predetermined stem cell population along the walls of forebrain ventricles generate neuronal precursors that migrate via the rostral migratory stream (RMS) into the center of the OB.
evidence: This describes the established migration pathway of neuronal precursors.

claim: After radial migration, cells integrate into the granule cell layer (GCL) and glomerular layers (GL).
source: After their radial migration into the principal target layers, the granule cell (GCL) and glomerular layers (GL), cells integrate into the preexisting circuitry and function as interneurons using GABA and dopamine as their principal neurotransmitters (Whitman and Greer, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Whitman and Greer, 2007.

claim: Integrated OB neurons function as interneurons using GABA and dopamine as their principal neurotransmitters.
source: After their radial migration into the principal target layers, the granule cell (GCL) and glomerular layers (GL), cells integrate into the preexisting circuitry and function as interneurons using GABA and dopamine as their principal neurotransmitters (Whitman and Greer, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Whitman and Greer, 2007.

claim: Neuronal integration in the adult OB is considered to be a competitive process.
source: First, neuronal integration in the adult is a competitive process, during which large numbers of newly arriving neurons compete for integration into the circuitry and ultimately survival.
evidence: This represents the prevailing model in the field that the authors are challenging.

claim: Competition for neuronal integration is thought to occur during a critical window of 2–8 weeks after arrival.
source: This competition is thought to occur during a defined critical window of 2–8 weeks after arrival and leads to the apoptotic elimination of about half of the initial population (Bergami and Berninger, 2012; Lledo et al., 2006; Mandairon et al., 2006; Petreanu and Alvarez-Buylla, 2002; Winner et al., 2002; Yamaguchi and Mori, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing the prevailing model.

claim: The competitive process leads to apoptotic elimination of about half of the initial neuron population.
source: This competition is thought to occur during a defined critical window of 2–8 weeks after arrival and leads to the apoptotic elimination of about half of the initial population (Bergami and Berninger, 2012; Lledo et al., 2006; Mandairon et al., 2006; Petreanu and Alvarez-Buylla, 2002; Winner et al., 2002; Yamaguchi and Mori, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations describing the prevailing model.

claim: The OB represents a turnover system in which newly integrating cells replace preexisting ones.
source: Second, the OB represents a turnover system, in which newly integrating cells replace preexisting ones, leading to a relatively stable total number of neurons in the target layers (Bergami and Berninger, 2012; Imayoshi et al., 2008; Lledo et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing the prevailing turnover model.

claim: The turnover system leads to a relatively stable total number of neurons in the target layers.
source: Second, the OB represents a turnover system, in which newly integrating cells replace preexisting ones, leading to a relatively stable total number of neurons in the target layers (Bergami and Berninger, 2012; Imayoshi et al., 2008; Lledo et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing the prevailing turnover model.

claim: The concepts of competitive selection and turnover are largely based on lineage-tracing experiments using thymidine analogs like BrdU or 3H-thymidine.
source: These two concepts are to a large extend based on lineage-tracing experiments using thymidine analogs like bromodeoxyuridine (BrdU) or 3H-thymidine to label the DNA of dividing cells (Mandairon et al., 2006; Petreanu and Alvarez-Buylla, 2002; Winner et al., 2002; Yamaguchi and Mori, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies using these methods.

claim: A common observation in thymidine analog experiments is a loss of labeled cells during the first few weeks after their arrival in the olfactory bulb.
source: A common observation in such experiments is a loss of labeled cells during the first few weeks after their arrival in the olfactory bulb, which led to the postulation of a selection mechanism allowing the remodeling of specific OB circuits during a period when new cells had already matured and developed dendritic arborizations (Petreanu and Alvarez-Buylla, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Petreanu and Alvarez-Buylla, 2002.

claim: Genetic approaches using CRE-inducible markers have demonstrated an accumulation of adult born neurons in the OB over time.
source: Alternatively, genetic approaches using CRE-inducible markers layers have been performed and demonstrated an accumulation of adult born neurons in the OB over time (Imayoshi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Imayoshi et al., 2008.

claim: The accumulation of adult born neurons has been interpreted as replacement of older neurons that died.
source: In agreement with the turnover model, this has been interpreted as a replacement of older neurons that died (Imayoshi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Imayoshi et al., 2008.

claim: Two-photon in vivo imaging allows studying OB neurons directly in the living animal.
source: Only recently more direct approaches based on two-photon in vivo imaging allowed studying OB neurons directly in the living animal (Mizrahi et al., 2006; Sailor et al., 2016; Wallace et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies using this technique.

claim: Long-term observation of juxtaglomerular neurons demonstrated an increase in these populations over time.
source: Interestingly, long-term observation of either juxtaglomerular neurons in general (Mizrahi et al., 2006), or more specifically of dopaminergic neurons, demonstrated an increase in these populations over time (Adam and Mizrahi, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mizrahi et al., 2006 and Adam and Mizrahi, 2011.

claim: The increase in juxtaglomerular neurons was interpreted as a change in the interneuron subtype composition of the OB.
source: While at first sight this finding contradicts a pure replacement model, it was interpreted as a change in the interneuron subtype composition of the OB (Adam and Mizrahi, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Adam and Mizrahi, 2011.

claim: Sensory deprivation by naris closure reduced the number of BrdU-labeled newborn neurons in the OB.
source: On one hand, sensory deprivation by naris closure reduced the number of BrdU-labeled newborn neurons in the OB (Mandairon et al., 2006; Saghatelyan et al., 2005; Yamaguchi and Mori, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Olfactory training increased the number of labeled neurons.
source: On the other hand, olfactory training increased the number of labeled neurons (Mouret et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mouret et al., 2008.

claim: Postnatal in vivo brain electroporation of the dorsal ventricular zone targets stem cell populations that generate neurons for the superficial layers of the OB.
source: Postnatal in vivo brain electroporation of the dorsal ventricular zone targets stem cell populations that generate neurons for the superficial layers of the OB (Figure 1a,b; de Chevigny et al., 2012b), which can be reliably reached by two-photon microscopy (Adam and Mizrahi, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to de Chevigny et al., 2012b and reference to Figure 1a,b.

claim: Three weeks after electroporation, OB-labeled neurons comprised 6% tyrosine hydroxylase expressing dopaminergic/GABAergic neurons.
source: Three weeks later, OB-labeled neurons comprised a mixed population of 6% tyrosine hydroxylase expressing dopaminergic/GABAergic neurons, 12% calretinin positive purely GABAergic neurons, 22% other GABAergic PGN (Figure 1b) and 60% mostly superficially positioned granule cells (GC).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Three weeks after electroporation, OB-labeled neurons comprised 12% calretinin positive purely GABAergic neurons.
source: Three weeks later, OB-labeled neurons comprised a mixed population of 6% tyrosine hydroxylase expressing dopaminergic/GABAergic neurons, 12% calretinin positive purely GABAergic neurons, 22% other GABAergic PGN (Figure 1b) and 60% mostly superficially positioned granule cells (GC).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Three weeks after electroporation, OB-labeled neurons comprised 22% other GABAergic PGN.
source: Three weeks later, OB-labeled neurons comprised a mixed population of 6% tyrosine hydroxylase expressing dopaminergic/GABAergic neurons, 12% calretinin positive purely GABAergic neurons, 22% other GABAergic PGN (Figure 1b) and 60% mostly superficially positioned granule cells (GC).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Three weeks after electroporation, OB-labeled neurons comprised 60% mostly superficially positioned granule cells.
source: Three weeks later, OB-labeled neurons comprised a mixed population of 6% tyrosine hydroxylase expressing dopaminergic/GABAergic neurons, 12% calretinin positive purely GABAergic neurons, 22% other GABAergic PGN (Figure 1b) and 60% mostly superficially positioned granule cells (GC).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: There was no detectable astroglia reaction after thinning and window implantation.
source: In agreement with previous observations (Xu et al., 2007), there was no detectable astroglia reaction or accumulation of microglia after thinning and window implantation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2007 and data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was no accumulation of microglia after thinning and window implantation.
source: In agreement with previous observations (Xu et al., 2007), there was no detectable astroglia reaction or accumulation of microglia after thinning and window implantation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2007 and data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Among 755 periglomerular neurons in 11 mice, only 5.1% were lost over the proposed critical period.
source: Among 755 periglomerular neurons (PGN) in 11 mice only 5.1% were lost over the proposed critical period (Figure 2a, see circles for lost cells no. 14 and 17 in Figure 1d,g).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2a and Figure 1d,g.

claim: The percentage of lost neurons was very similar between individual animals.
source: The percentage of lost neurons was very similar between individual animals and was independent of the density of labeled cells in the observation window (between 18 and 100 neurons; Figure 2a).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The percentage of lost neurons was independent of the density of labeled cells in the observation window.
source: The percentage of lost neurons was very similar between individual animals and was independent of the density of labeled cells in the observation window (between 18 and 100 neurons; Figure 2a).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Out of 178 RFP positive granule neurons observed between 3 and 8 weeks after their birth, not a single cell disappeared.
source: Out of 178 RFP positive neurons observed between 3 and 8 weeks after their birth not a single cell disappeared over the subsequent imaging sessions (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Perinatally generated OB interneurons in both the GL and the GCL are rarely eliminated after arrival in terminal positions.
source: We conclude that perinatally generated OB interneurons in both, the GL and the GCL are rarely eliminated after arrival in terminal positions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on perinatal neurons.

claim: One week after tamoxifen induction, virtually all RFP-positive cells in the RMS expressed the immature neuron marker doublecortin.
source: One week after induction virtually all RFP-positive cells in the RMS and about 30% in the OB layers expressed the immature neuron marker doublecortin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c,d.

claim: One week after tamoxifen induction, about 30% of RFP-positive cells in the OB layers expressed the immature neuron marker doublecortin.
source: One week after induction virtually all RFP-positive cells in the RMS and about 30% in the OB layers expressed the immature neuron marker doublecortin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1c,d).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1c,d.

claim: Analyses of 538 periglomerular neurons in eight adult animals showed that only 1.5% disappeared over the 7 weeks period after their first identification.
source: Analyses of 538 periglomerular neurons of the first cohort in eight animals showed that only 1.5% disappeared over the 7 weeks period after their first identification (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: During the 8 weeks observation window of adult born granule neurons in Nestin Cre-ERT2/Rosa-RFP mice, six out of 101 neurons disappeared (5.9%).
source: We observed 101 adult born neurons in nine animals (Figure 3a,b,c). During the 8 weeks observation window, six neurons disappeared (5,9%).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3a,b,c.

claim: Tracing of 48 adult-born GCs labeled with lentivirus led to the identification of only a single cell that disappeared (2.1%) during the 7 weeks observation period.
source: Tracing of 48 adult-born GCs in 19 fields of view from three mice led to the identification of only a single cell that disappeared (2.1%; Figure 3e) during the 7 weeks observation period.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Under physiological conditions, cell loss in adult born OB neurons during the proposed critical selection period was very low, comparable to the findings for perinatally born neurons.
source: Thus, overall under physiological conditions cell loss in adult born OB neurons during the proposed critical selection period was very low, comparable to the findings for perinatally born neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on adult and perinatal neurons.

claim: Naris closure in adult Nestin Cre-ERT2/Rosa-RFP mice resulted in a significant increase in cell loss.
source: Analysis of RFP-positive PGN over the following 8 weeks revealed a significant increase in cell loss (Figure 4bc; p=0.03, four control and three occluded animals, 151 cells).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4bc with statistical significance p=0.03.

claim: Under physiological conditions, newly born neurons in the perinatal and adult OB show little cell loss after arrival in the OB.
source: In conclusion, under physiological conditions newly born neurons in the perinatal and adult OB show little cell loss after arrival in the OB.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Significant cell loss during the observation period was found after blocking sensory input.
source: However, significant cell loss during this observation period was found after blocking sensory input, demonstrating that cell death could be detected with our approach.
evidence: This is based on the naris occlusion experiment data.

claim: Using four i.p. injections of 50 mg/kg BrdU every 2 hr into adult mice, an approximately 40% loss of labeled neurons in the OB was found between 2 and 6 weeks in the GL as well as in the GCL.
source: Indeed, using four i.p. injections of 50 mg/kg BrdU every 2 hr into adult mice, we found an approximately 40% loss of labeled neurons in the OB between 2 and 6 weeks in the GL as well as in the GCL (Figure 5ab).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5ab.

claim: BrdU+ cell number in the dorsal OB showed the same 40% loss that was found in the entire bulb.
source: BrdU+ cell number in the dorsal OB showed the same 40% loss that was found in the entire bulb (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Four injections of 50 mg/kg EdU in 2-month-old mice led to an about 40% loss of labeled cells in the GL and the GCL of the OB between 2 and 6 weeks.
source: Four injections of 50 mg/kg EdU in 2-month-old mice led to an about 40% loss of labeled cells in the GL and the GCL of the OB between 2 and 6 weeks, highly comparable to the results based on BrdU (Figure 5c,e).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5c,e.

claim: Four injections of 1 or 5 mg/kg EdU led to the detection of slightly lower amounts of newly generated cells in the OB layers after 2 weeks.
source: Four injection of 1 or 5 mg/kg EdU under the same conditions led to the detection of slightly lower amounts of newly generated cells in the OB layers after 2 weeks (Figure 5de).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5de.

claim: At 1 or 5 mg/kg EdU, the decrease in cell numbers between 2 and 6 weeks was not detectable, both in the GL and the GCL.
source: Importantly, under these conditions the decrease in cell numbers between 2 and 6 weeks was not detectable anymore, both in the GL and the GCL (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: Deep and superficial GCs showed the same behavior: cell loss at high EdU dose and survival at 5 mg/kg.
source: However, deep and superficial GCs showed the same behavior, cell loss at high EdU dose and survival at 5 mg/kg, as the entire GCL (Figure 5f).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Loss of labeled cells in the OB during the critical period is correlated with the concentration of modified nucleotides in the DNA of newborn OB neurons.
source: Altogether, these results lead to the conclusion that loss of labeled cells in the OB during the critical period is correlated with the concentration of modified nucleotides in the DNA of newborn OB neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EdU dose-response experiments.

claim: Analyses of immunostained tissues detected consistently low numbers of CC3 positive cells in the OB layers (363 ± 34 cells /mm3).
source: Analyses of immunostained tissues detected consistently low numbers of CC3 positive cells in the OB layers (363 ± 34 cells /mm3 n = 15; thus about 940 CC3+ cells/GCL) in overall agreement with previous work (770 cells/GCL; Yamaguchi and Mori, 2005).
evidence: This is based on experimental data with n=15 and is in agreement with citation to Yamaguchi and Mori, 2005.

claim: Among the 10803 analyzed EdU-positive OB neurons, only 26 showed co-labeling for CC3.
source: However, among the 10803 analyzed EdU-positive OB neurons only 26 showed co-labeling for CC3.
evidence: This is based on experimental data analyzing EdU and CC3 co-labeling.

claim: Application of four times 5 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg EdU had no influence on the percentage of double stained cells (EdU and CC3).
source: Application of four times 5 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg EdU had no influence on the percentage of double stained cells, indicating that thymidine analog induced toxicity did not pass via the apoptotic pathway (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5h.

claim: Thymidine analog induced toxicity did not pass via the apoptotic pathway.
source: Application of four times 5 mg/kg or 50 mg/kg EdU had no influence on the percentage of double stained cells, indicating that thymidine analog induced toxicity did not pass via the apoptotic pathway (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of change in CC3/EdU co-labeling at different EdU doses.

claim: Density of CC3-positive cells was more than six times higher in the RMS than in the GCL and the GL.
source: Interestingly, density of CC3-positive cells was more than six times higher in the RMS than in the GCL and the GL (Figure 5i).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 5i.

claim: The finding that CC3-positive cells are more abundant in the RMS is in good agreement with previous data.
source: This is in good agreement with previous data (Biebl et al., 2000) and suggests that cell death in the system occurs predominantly at the precursor level.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Biebl et al., 2000.

claim: Cell death in the OB neurogenesis system occurs predominantly at the precursor level.
source: This is in good agreement with previous data (Biebl et al., 2000) and suggests that cell death in the system occurs predominantly at the precursor level.
evidence: This is inferred from the higher density of CC3-positive cells in the RMS compared to OB layers.

claim: Lineage tracing by high doses of thymidine analogs is associated with cell loss in the OB.
source: In conclusion, the above results, showing that lineage tracing by high doses of thymidine analogs is associated with cell loss in the OB, point to toxicity of such DNA modifying agents.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the EdU dose-response experiments.

claim: At low EdU doses, cell loss in the OB during the proposed critical selection period is not detected.
source: Moreover, the finding that at low EdU doses cell loss in the OB during the proposed critical selection period is notdetected represents an independent confirmation of our in vivo imaging based findings.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from low-dose EdU experiments.

claim: Continuous long-term observations of perinatally generated PGN and GC provided no evidence for sustained cell loss after the initial 8 weeks time window.
source: Continuous long-term observations of perinatally generated PGN and GC provided no evidence for sustained cell loss after the initial 8 weeks time window (Figure 6a,b).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6a,b.

claim: Adult generated GC or PGN showed stability when observed for up to 24 weeks after their generation.
source: The same stability of the labeled population was evident when adult generated GC or PGN were observed for up to 24 weeks after their generation (Figure 6c,d).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6c,d.

claim: CRE-induced recombination in Nestin-CRE-ERT2 mice occurs often at the stem cell level.
source: Moreover, as CRE-induced recombination in Nestin-CRE-ERT2 mice occurs often at the stem cell level (Imayoshi et al., 2008), recombined stem cells continued to generate new neurons.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Imayoshi et al., 2008.

claim: Additional adult born neurons permanently appeared in the observation window.
source: In agreement, additional adult born neurons permanently appeared in the observation window (Figure 6e), leading to a more than doubling of the neuron population of adult generated PGN over an observation period of six months (Figure 6f).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: The neuron population of adult generated PGN more than doubled over an observation period of six months.
source: In agreement, additional adult born neurons permanently appeared in the observation window (Figure 6e), leading to a more than doubling of the neuron population of adult generated PGN over an observation period of six months (Figure 6f).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: Over time, slightly larger image frames were necessary to accommodate the same group of neurons in Z-maximum projections of the GCL and GL.
source: First, we asked if a volume increase in the OB could be detected directly in the living brain during in vivo imaging experiments. We found that over time slightly larger image frames were necessary to accommodate the same group of neurons in our Z-maximum projections of the GCL and GL (Figure 1d; Figure 3a; Figure 1—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: This is based on observations from in vivo imaging data shown in multiple figures.

claim: Volumetric analysis of inter-neuronal space demonstrated that distance between neurons increased steadily between 2 and 5 months.
source: Indeed, volumetric analysis of inter-neuronal space between groups of four neurons in X, Y, Z (thus an irregular pyramid) demonstrated that distance between neurons increased steadily between 2 and 5 months (Figures 7a,b and 4 animals at each time point), strongly indicating continuous OB growth.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figures 7a,b.

claim: Volumetric analysis based on 3D reconstructions of cleared OBs revealed a steady increase in OB size leading to a significant 44% enlargement of the structure from 2 to 12 months.
source: Volumetric analysis based on 3D reconstructions of cleared OBs (Figure 7c,d and Video 3) revealed a steady increase in OB size leading to a significant 44% enlargement of the structure from 2 to 12 months (Figure 7d,e).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7c,d,e and Video 3.

claim: The volume increase in the OB affected equally the granule and the glomerular layers.
source: This volume increase affected equally the granule and the glomerular layers (Figure 7f) in the absence of obvious changes in layer repartition (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7f and Figure 7—figure supplement 1a.

claim: During the interval from 2 to 12 months, total forebrain volume was unchanged.
source: During the same interval, total forebrain volume was unchanged (Figure 7g).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7g.

claim: The density of nuclei in the GCL was highly stable at all observed time points.
source: Quantification revealed that the density of nuclei was highly stable at all observed time points (Figure 7h,i) while the density of astrocytes decreased and microglia density was unchanged (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a, b and c).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7h,i.

claim: The density of astrocytes decreased over time.
source: Quantification revealed that the density of nuclei was highly stable at all observed time points (Figure 7h,i) while the density of astrocytes decreased and microglia density was unchanged (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a, b and c).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1a, b and c.

claim: Microglia density was unchanged over time.
source: Quantification revealed that the density of nuclei was highly stable at all observed time points (Figure 7h,i) while the density of astrocytes decreased and microglia density was unchanged (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a, b and c).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1a, b and c.

claim: Both in vivo brain imaging and light sheet microscopy of fixed cleared tissue demonstrate that the mouse OB grows significantly during adult life in the absence of detectable changes in cell density.
source: Thus, both in vivo brain imaging and light sheet microscopy of fixed cleared tissue demonstrate that the mouse OB grows significantly during adult life in the absence of detectable changes in cell density.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data using both imaging approaches.

claim: Between 2 and 6 months, about 8000 cells/day are added to the growing OB.
source: Our data, based on measurements of cell density and volume of the structure, allows to estimate that between 2 and 6 months about 8000 cells/day are added to the growing OB.
evidence: This is calculated from the experimental data on cell density and volume.

claim: Using a genetic approach, Imayoshi et al found that 6 months after tamoxifen induction, labeled neurons represent 41.2% of the total population.
source: Interestingly, using a genetic approach, Imayoshi et al found that 6 months after tamoxifen induction, labeled neurons represent 41.2% of the total population (1,500,000, thus 620,000 new neurons).
evidence: This is based on citation to work by Imayoshi et al.

claim: Considering 60–70% recombination efficiency at the stem cell level, the genetic approach leads to a number of almost 6000 new cells that are added per day.
source: Considering 60–70% recombination efficiency at the stem cell level (Imayoshi et al., 2008), this leads to a number of almost 6000 new cells that are added per day.
evidence: This is calculated from data cited from Imayoshi et al., 2008.

claim: Direct measurements and the genetic approach render highly comparable results in terms of the number of neurons that integrates in the adult OB.
source: Thus, our direct measurements and the genetic approach render highly comparable results in terms of the number of neurons that integrates in the adult OB.
evidence: This is a comparison between the authors' data and cited genetic approach data.

claim: The level of neuronal cell death among perinatal and adult born interneurons after their arrival in terminal positions in the OB is very low.
source: First, the level of neuronal cell death among perinatal and adult born interneurons after their arrival in terminal positions in the OB is very low.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on in vivo imaging data.

claim: Adult OB neurogenesis is not a homeostatic but an addition process.
source: Second, adult OB neurogenesis is not a homeostatic but an addition process.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on growth and survival data.

claim: Classical lineage tracing approaches based on thymidine analogs are associated with unwanted side effects.
source: Third, classical lineage tracing approaches based on thymidine analogs are associated with unwanted side effects and have to be interpreted with care.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on dose-response experiments.

claim: Both BrdU and 3H-dT are toxic.
source: However, both BrdU and 3H-dT are toxic (Breunig et al., 2007; Ehmann et al., 1975; Kolb et al., 1999; Kuwagata et al., 2007; Nowakowski and Hayes, 2000; Sekerková et al., 2004; Taupin, 2007) and studies in both rodents (Lehner et al., 2011; Webster et al., 1973) and primates (Duque and Rakic, 2011) pointed to unwanted, and hard to interpret, long term effects associated to their use.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies documenting toxicity.

claim: Studies in rodents and primates pointed to unwanted, and hard to interpret, long term effects associated with BrdU and 3H-dT use.
source: However, both BrdU and 3H-dT are toxic (Breunig et al., 2007; Ehmann et al., 1975; Kolb et al., 1999; Kuwagata et al., 2007; Nowakowski and Hayes, 2000; Sekerková et al., 2004; Taupin, 2007) and studies in both rodents (Lehner et al., 2011; Webster et al., 1973) and primates (Duque and Rakic, 2011) pointed to unwanted, and hard to interpret, long term effects associated to their use.
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies in rodents and primates.

claim: A selection step in which an overproduced precursor population is matched to the needs of the target structure does not principally occur after arrival in the OB.
source: These results lead to the conclusion that a selection step in which an overproduced precursor population is matched to the needs of the target structure, does not principally occur after arrival in the OB.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the low cell death observed in the OB layers.

claim: In Bax-KO mice, in which apoptotic cell death is blocked, the general structure and size of the OB neuron layers are virtually unaffected.
source: For example, in Bax-KO mice, in which apoptotic cell death is blocked, the general structure and size of the OB neuron layers are virtually unaffected (Kim et al., 2007) while a disorganization and accumulation of neuronal precursors in the RMS was observed.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kim et al., 2007.

claim: In Bax-KO mice, a disorganization and accumulation of neuronal precursors in the RMS was observed.
source: For example, in Bax-KO mice, in which apoptotic cell death is blocked, the general structure and size of the OB neuron layers are virtually unaffected (Kim et al., 2007) while a disorganization and accumulation of neuronal precursors in the RMS was observed.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kim et al., 2007.

claim: Neuronal selection may occur more at the level of recruitment from the RMS than at the level of integration in the target layers.
source: This points to the possibility that neuronal selection occurs more at the level of recruitment from the RMS than at the level of integration in the target layers.
evidence: This is speculated based on the Bax-KO data and CC3 distribution.

claim: In developing cortical interneurons, neuronal survival is largely independent of signals from the local environment.
source: It has been shown that in developing cortical interneurons neuronal survival is largely independent of signals from the local environment but that about 40% of the total population is predestined to undergo Bax-dependent apoptosis (Southwell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Southwell et al., 2012.

claim: About 40% of developing cortical interneurons are predestined to undergo Bax-dependent apoptosis.
source: It has been shown that in developing cortical interneurons neuronal survival is largely independent of signals from the local environment but that about 40% of the total population is predestined to undergo Bax-dependent apoptosis (Southwell et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Southwell et al., 2012.

claim: If neuronal death is intrinsically encoded, cell death would be expected to occur already in the SVZ/RMS.
source: In such a scenario, cell death would be expected to occur already in the SVZ/RMS.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the intrinsic encoding hypothesis.

claim: Neuronal death is a rare event not only during early stages after arrival in the OB, but at all observed time points.
source: Our results demonstrate that neuronal death is a rare event not only during early stages after arrival in the OB, but at all observed time points.
evidence: This is based on long-term in vivo imaging data.

claim: The permanent addition of new neurons in the absence of considerable cell removal is not compatible with the idea that the OB represents a turnover system of constant size.
source: However, the permanent addition of new neurons in the absence of considerable cell removal is not compatible with the idea that the OB represents a turnover system of constant size (Bergami and Berninger, 2012; Imayoshi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a logical inference from the data showing neuronal addition without death.

claim: Growth of the adult OB in mice has been observed in other studies.
source: Indeed, growth of the adult OB in mice has been observed in other studies, although considerable variation and dependence on genetic background have been reported (Mirich et al., 2002; Richard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mirich et al., 2002 and Richard et al., 2010.

claim: Other studies did not find obvious differences in total OB size or specific sublayers.
source: Other studies did not find obvious differences in total OB size or specific sublayers (Imayoshi et al., 2008; Petreanu and Alvarez-Buylla, 2002; Pomeroy et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies that did not observe OB growth.

claim: Past approaches to measuring OB size were based on 2D analysis of a subset of tissue sections and extrapolation of total volume.
source: Past approaches were based on the 2D analysis of a subset of tissue sections and the extrapolation of the total volume based thereon.
evidence: This describes the methodology of previous studies.

claim: Light sheet microscopy is suited to overcome limitations of 2D sectioning approaches because the OB is imaged and measured in its entirety.
source: Light sheet microscopy is suited to overcome many of these limitations as the OB is imaged and measured in its entirety.
evidence: This is a methodological advantage of the light sheet approach.

claim: During in vivo long-term observations, constantly larger frames are needed to accommodate the same group of cells.
source: Independently from the light-sheet approach, we show that during in vivo long-term observations constantly larger frames are needed to accommodate the same group of cells and that the distance of individually identified neurons measurably increases.
evidence: This is based on in vivo imaging observations.

claim: The distance of individually identified neurons measurably increases over time.
source: Independently from the light-sheet approach, we show that during in vivo long-term observations constantly larger frames are needed to accommodate the same group of cells and that the distance of individually identified neurons measurably increases.
evidence: This is based on in vivo imaging observations.

claim: The finding that distance between neurons increases is in full agreement with the observation that the distance between specific glomeruli increases with age of the animal.
source: The latter finding is in full agreement with the observation that the distance between specific glomeruli increases with age of the animal (Richard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Richard et al., 2010.

claim: Neuronal cell death is rare in the OB.
source: In conclusion, we show here that neuronal cell death is rare in the OB and that neuronal addition, but not replacement, is the outcome of adult neurogenesis.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Neuronal addition, but not replacement, is the outcome of adult neurogenesis in the OB.
source: In conclusion, we show here that neuronal cell death is rare in the OB and that neuronal addition, but not replacement, is the outcome of adult neurogenesis.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Genetic fate mapping studies pointed toward an increase in specific neuronal subsets in the adult OB.
source: Genetic fate mapping studies (Ninkovic et al., 2007) and also direct observation of the TH positive neuron population (Adam and Mizrahi, 2011) already pointed toward an increase in specific neuronal subsets in the adult OB.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ninkovic et al., 2007 and Adam and Mizrahi, 2011.

claim: Direct observation of the TH positive neuron population pointed toward an increase in specific neuronal subsets in the adult OB.
source: Genetic fate mapping studies (Ninkovic et al., 2007) and also direct observation of the TH positive neuron population (Adam and Mizrahi, 2011) already pointed toward an increase in specific neuronal subsets in the adult OB.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Adam and Mizrahi, 2011.

claim: Neuronal addition is a general phenomenon that affects perinatally and adult generated neurons, leading to substantial growth of the OB throughout life.
source: We show that neuronal addition is a general phenomenon that affects perinatally and adult generated neurons, leading to substantial growth of the OB throughout life.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's data on both perinatal and adult neurons.

claim: OB neurogenesis appears to reflect ongoing brain development rather than homeostasis.
source: Thus, OB neurogenesis appears to reflect ongoing brain development rather than homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the finding of neuronal addition without replacement.

claim: An increase in BrdU-positive cells in the GCL was observed in BAX conditional mutant mice.
source: Moreover, an increase in BrdU-positive cells in the GCL was observed in BAX conditional mutant mice (Kim et al., 2007; Sahay et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2007 and Sahay et al., 2011.

claim: Neuronal selection at the level of integration has been proposed to underlie adult hippocampal neurogenesis.
source: Finally, neuronal selection at the level of integration has been proposed to underlie adult hippocampal neurogenesis (Bergami and Berninger, 2012; Buss et al., 2006), and recent in vivo observations indicate that most cell death occurs among immature neurons, at relatively early stages after their birth (Pilz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bergami and Berninger, 2012 and Buss et al., 2006.

claim: Recent in vivo observations indicate that most cell death in hippocampal neurogenesis occurs among immature neurons, at relatively early stages after their birth.
source: Finally, neuronal selection at the level of integration has been proposed to underlie adult hippocampal neurogenesis (Bergami and Berninger, 2012; Buss et al., 2006), and recent in vivo observations indicate that most cell death occurs among immature neurons, at relatively early stages after their birth (Pilz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pilz et al., 2018.

claim: The finding that most hippocampal cell death occurs at early stages correlates well with the quasi absence of death during later stages observed in the OB.
source: This correlates well with the quasi absence of death during later stages, that we observe in the OB.
evidence: This is an inference connecting hippocampal data to the OB findings.

claim: Most OB interneurons are generated during the perinatal period.
source: We first focused on the perinatal period, when most OB interneurons are generated (Batista-Brito et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Batista-Brito et al., 2008.

claim: Loss of new neurons in the OB after arrival at terminal positions occurs only at low levels.
source: We show that loss of new neurons in the OB after arrival at terminal positions occurs only at low levels.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract based on in vivo imaging data.

claim: Long-term observations showed that no substantial cell death occurred at later stages.
source: Moreover, long-term observations showed that no substantial cell death occurred at later stages.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract based on long-term in vivo imaging data.

claim: Neuronal death was induced by standard doses of thymidine analogs.
source: Neuronal death was induced by standard doses of thymidine analogs, but disappeared when low doses were used.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract based on EdU dose-response experiments.

claim: Neuronal death disappeared when low doses of thymidine analogs were used.
source: Neuronal death was induced by standard doses of thymidine analogs, but disappeared when low doses were used.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract based on EdU dose-response experiments.

claim: The OB grows throughout life.
source: Finally, we demonstrate that the OB grows throughout life.
evidence: This is a main finding stated in the abstract based on in vivo imaging and light sheet microscopy data.

claim: Neuronal selection during OB-neurogenesis does not occur after neurons reached stable positions.
source: This shows that neuronal selection during OB-neurogenesis does not occur after neurons reached stable positions.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the low cell death observed.

claim: OB neurogenesis does not represent neuronal turnover but lifelong neuronal addition.
source: Moreover, this suggests that OB neurogenesis does not represent neuronal turnover but lifelong neuronal addition.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the growth and survival data.
